ideas.title: Narrative is the recurrent locus of editorial hierarchy drift — make Narrative the primary control point for company‑first framing
ideas.description: Across experiments 007–009 the Narrative stage is the most common first-visible place where a company-first editorial hierarchy breaks and unsupported claims are introduced. Prioritizing a Narrative-focused gate or intervention offers the strongest, evidence-backed opportunity to prevent downstream reframing toward product/technical-first stories.
ideas.audience: Internal content/experiment teams, prompt engineers, editorial leads working on Nuëyon.Compose pipeline orchestration and quality control.
ideas.rationale: Why it matters: The report documents Narrative as the first observable hierarchy shift in many runs (007 runs 001–002; 008 A-002; 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003). Because Narrative directly crafts the reader-facing through-line, targeting it can block recurring downstream amplifications in Compose. Gaps and uncertainty: Narrative is not the sole origin — some runs show Idea or Synthesis as the first drift (e.g., 007 candidate 003, 008 Idea-origin runs), so a Narrative-only fix may not eliminate all failures. A controlled test is required to confirm impact and to avoid missing upstream causes.
ideas.evidence: Explicit statements in the report: “Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.” Localized examples: Experiment 007 — Narrative first in candidate 001–002; Experiment 008 A-002 — Narrative invents founders and product leads; Experiment 009 — Narrative is the first clear editorial shift in baseline 002 and 003 and in candidate 001–003. The report also notes that Narrative failures then persist into Compose in multiple runs.
